components.label: Breath as the key: global shift established, local necessity untested (VASO-C013, VASO-C004, VASO-C039, VASO-C011)
components.note: Slow breathing shifts autonomic balance globally (VASO-C013, well supported); the felt release on an exhale is proponent testimony (VASO-C004); the two-key necessity is unresolved, with a pressure-only protocol that carried no breathing instruction beside it (VASO-C039); the seconds-scale state-not-structure inference stands on priors, its premise unmeasured (VASO-C011).

components.label: The perforator alternative: stuck cutaneous vessel-nerve bundles held by tone, collar and tether (VASO-C174, VASO-C143, VASO-C077)
components.note: A genuinely different mechanism with cheap tests, held entirely on a self-published AI-generated essay the ledger has not been able to read; its write mechanism (regional skin vasoconstriction) and the reversibility timescale of fascial densification are anchor-only. Featured for stakes, graded for what it has: nothing yet in either direction.

components.label: Blood and mind: hemo-neural modulation, attention's write channel, vascular memory and the contemplative maps (VASO-C012, VASO-C006, VASO-C021, VASO-C022)
components.note: Vascular mechanics modulate neurons instantaneously in rat brain (VASO-C012) and attention regulates a peripheral vascular bed over minutes without arousal (VASO-C006); neither shows storage or content-specific readout, which the memory attribution requires and no record supplies (VASO-C021). The contemplative-map identification rests on one uncited assertion in the essay (VASO-C022).

researchPriority.reason: The decisive experiments are specified, cheap and unrun: a time-locked imaging study of a single release, and a breath-randomized repeat of a compression protocol that already exists, would each settle the central crux in one study, and either outcome would produce ordinary useful musculoskeletal science. The census that would replace the case's opening premise with a measurement has never been attempted.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on hypothesis statements alone — Johnson's three vasocomputation hypotheses (VASO-E013) and the essay's relay of the clinging-as-latch identification (VASO-E038), both context — and qualified by the critical report's write–store–read test (VASO-E017): biological memory requires state that depends on prior input, can be read out later and discriminates prior inputs, and the latch literature addresses none of these. No admitted record shows a vascular state encoding, persisting and biasing later neural processing in a content-specific way; the nearest precedent the report names is a slime mold. The supporting mechanism rungs (VASO-C010, VASO-C012) are credible but establish only the weak form — vascular state is part of the neural state-space.

treatment.plainLanguage: The theory's biggest idea: that tension held in blood-vessel walls stores something the mind later uses — a prediction, an expectation, a grasp — and that the Buddhist notion of clinging is what that storage feels like from inside.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: There is no evidence record in either direction, so the claim currently decides nothing; if the animal write–store–read experiment returned a history-specific neural bias it would establish a new memory mechanism, and a clean negative would collapse strong vasocomputation to ordinary neurovascular physiology.
treatment.strongestObjection: Hysteresis is not memory: a thermostat holds state after its input changes without having an autobiography, and every established piece — neurovascular coupling, latch economy, mechanosensitive modulation — is necessary but not sufficient for a vessel to store a thought.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An animal preparation in which different induced vascular states produce reliably different later neural responses under identical stimulation with oxygenation clamped (VASO-R005).
A demonstration that a maintained vascular state, after its initiating neural input stops, biases neural responses back toward the trained pattern.
Conversely, a clean finding that vascular manipulation affects neural gain only through instantaneous perfusion, with no history dependence once those variables are equalized.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The two linchpins — an objective seconds-scale release and a vascular releasing element — have no direct evidence located in either direction (VASO-E016). Where the thesis names its compartment, the record leans against it: pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles hold constriction with maintained or rising phosphorylation, the opposite of a dephosphorylated latch (VASO-E020), and no arteriole's energetic cost has ever been measured, so the economy argument rests on conduit arteries (VASO-E019). The Doppler pattern near trigger points is recorded as weak support at zero diagnosticity because its authors list contracture compression as a co-equal cause (VASO-E027). The remaining records are the hypothesis stated by its proponents (VASO-E013, VASO-E037) and the second essay's relocation of the vascular element away from the arteriole (VASO-E044, VASO-E045), the latter from a source the ledger has not read. Unresolved rather than contradicted because none of the arteriole studies withdrew its stimulus, so input-free persistence has not been tested.

treatment.plainLanguage: A knot is a tiny blood vessel inside the muscle locked shut by its own smooth muscle, starving the tissue around it, and the acid, ache and muscle guarding follow from that — rather than the knot being damaged or scarred tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the thesis the case grades; a demonstrated latch at a tender point, or a blood-first release, would decide the case for the vascular account, and a hot knot on PET or a non-latching arteriolar phenotype throughout would decide it against.
treatment.strongestObjection: The one tissue compartment the hypothesis names has been examined with the right molecular readout and shows sustained activation, not an economical hold; the vessels with abnormal Doppler are conduit-scale and their behaviour fits mechanical compression by contracted fibre; and the only imaged within-session disappearance of a trigger point was produced by pressure with breathing uninstructed.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole holding constriction after its stimulus is withdrawn, at falling phosphorylation and measured low energetic cost (VASO-R004).
Time-resolved imaging showing perfusion rising before stiffness falls at a felt release, exceeding sham and pressure-only controls (VASO-R001).
A palpated knot stiff on elastography, active on EMG and metabolically cold on FDG-PET (VASO-R013).
Against: elevated FDG uptake at knots, the non-latching phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles, or equal clearance of points under held breath.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone, in SRC-JHONG-2026A, a self-published AI-generated essay the ledger has not been able to read and verify; no admitted evidence record bears on it. The account is a genuine alternative mechanism — vessel tone, a hyaluronan collar and a fascial tether as three nested memory elements — but each element is asserted, not measured, and it must also explain why the stiff regions blinded sonographers image lie inside the muscle (VASO-E087 on VASO-C182) rather than in the superficial fascia.

treatment.plainLanguage: On the rival vascular picture, what holds a knot is not one thing but three: the tone of a small skin-bound artery, a gel collar of hyaluronan around the vessel-and-nerve bundle where it pierces the fascia, and the tether that collar makes between the fascial sheet and the tissue beneath.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If tender points sit on Doppler-mapped perforators above chance and hydrodissection releases them without breath, the case moves to this account; a null coincidence map dissolves it in an afternoon.
treatment.strongestObjection: Nothing has been measured: the only source is an unread proponent essay, and the one instrumented pattern the ledger holds — stiff regions inside the trapezius and gastrocnemius — fits the intramuscular picture better than a bundle under the skin.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded palpated tender points coinciding with pencil-Doppler perforators above chance (VASO-R015).
Release of a tender point by ultrasound-guided saline hydrodissection at its perforator with no breath and no pressure (VASO-R017).
A local skin-perfusion flash time-locked to the exhale and the felt star, absent at sham sites and under inhale-hold (VASO-R016).
Against: tender points on perforators no more often than chance, or perfusion changes that are global and CO2-tracking.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The sole record is the founding essay's uncited assertion that the traditional maps place important knots along the torso midline and limbs (VASO-E039), which supplies no coding rule and no chance baseline. No blinded anatomical coding exists, so every apparent convergence is vulnerable to post-hoc matching; and even a genuine alignment with vascular geography would not show that anything latches or clenches.

treatment.plainLanguage: The Tibetan channel-knots, Hindu granthis and Chinese tender ashi points are read as maps made from inside by highly trained practitioners of the same vascular-autonomic tension system the case examines.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Even a positive blinded alignment would be evidence that the traditions mapped something anatomical, not that the something is a vascular state; a null would retire the convergence argument without touching the physiology.
treatment.strongestObjection: Resemblance found after the fact is the weakest kind of evidence, and nobody has coded the traditional locations under blinded rules or tested them against chance.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A preregistered, blinded coding of rtsa mdud, granthi and ashi locations aligning with vascular branch points, sympathetic chains or dense-fascia geography above chance (VASO-R006).
The same coding finding no alignment above chance.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hai and Murphy's kinetic model reproduces high sustained stress at low myosin phosphorylation — economical force maintenance after activation subsides — in vascular smooth-muscle preparations (VASO-E003, strong). Qualified by the case's own study: the one paired vessel-branch comparison found latch behaviour in the rabbit femoral artery and a forty-percent stress loss in its saphenous branch, attributed to motor-protein isoforms that do not support latch bridges, and nobody has followed the comparison downstream (VASO-E021). The essay's restatement (VASO-E034) overstates the model — low, not zero, activation — and adds no weight.

treatment.plainLanguage: Smooth muscle in blood-vessel walls can lock its molecular motors and hold tension cheaply after the signal telling it to contract has faded — textbook physiology since 1988.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Real but expected by every account; the latch existing in conduit arteries says nothing about whether it operates at a tender point, and the paired comparison shows it is not generic across vessel types.
treatment.strongestObjection: The demonstration record is concentrated in large tonic conduit preparations at zero transmural pressure, and the only downstream comparison lost the behaviour one branch order later.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A paired-caliber pressurized preparation showing latch capacity persisting into skeletal-muscle arterioles, or disappearing (VASO-R004).
Independent replication of the femoral/saphenous divergence.

claimAssessments.reasoning: A conditional inference graded on physiological priors: structural remodeling takes days to weeks, so a change completing in seconds would be a change of maintained state. The essay states the argument (VASO-E035); the trapezius pilot shows trigger-point area and pulsatility falling over visits after needling, not seconds (VASO-E030, context). The premise — an objective local event within seconds — is the unmeasured thing, and 'state' includes guarding and fascial densification as well as vessels.

treatment.plainLanguage: If a tender point really lets go within seconds, what let go must have been something the body was actively doing, not scar tissue that had to be remodeled.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Decides state against scar — which all three live accounts already accept — but not which state or which tissue, so it separates the featured hypothesis from the conventional one only if the seconds-scale premise is measured.
treatment.strongestObjection: The antecedent has never been observed; the closest the ledger comes is a stiff focus disappearing over a session of minutes under thumb pressure, and a fast non-vascular state (densification thinning, guarding switching off) satisfies the conditional as well as a vessel.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved elastography showing a stiffness step-drop within seconds of a felt release, exceeding sham (VASO-R001).
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition, which would leave the conditional true but idle.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone — the founding essay's statement of the Stecco group's densification model — with no admitted evidence record; the primary literature has not been retrieved, and the timescale of reversal under pressure, movement or warmth is unrecorded. It matters because a seconds-scale reversible fascial state would be a fast, non-vascular competitor to the latch account.

treatment.plainLanguage: Fascia researchers propose that the hyaluronan lubricant between fascial layers can thicken into a gel and then thin again under pressure, movement and warmth — a stiffness that comes and goes without any vessel involved.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If densification reverses within a session, the vascular attribution loses its claim to be the only fast mechanism and the keystone experiment needs the perfusion channel to discriminate; if reversal takes minutes to hours, the vascular account remains the sole candidate for a seconds-scale release.
treatment.strongestObjection: Nothing in the ledger measures the timescale, and the critical report notes the densification literature is largely anatomical and cadaveric rather than a demonstration that a painful point consists of reversible hyaluronan aggregation.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Retrieved primary studies reporting hyaluronan viscosity or fascial glide changing reversibly under load or warmth, with the timescale (VASO-R008).
Elastography showing a stiffness drop at a release with no accompanying perfusion change.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Proposed as a hypothesis in 2008 (VASO-E004, context) and given a demonstrated mechanism in 2024: physiological blood-pressure pulsations modulate central neuronal activity through mechanosensitive ion channels in rat preparations and awake animals (VASO-E005, strong). The demonstration is instantaneous modulation in brain, not storage and not the periphery, so the claim as stated is supported while its extension to peripheral tender points remains argument.

treatment.plainLanguage: Blood vessels do not only feed neurons; their mechanical state can nudge what nearby neurons do, moment to moment.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Establishes the read path of the vasocomputation loop in principle but is compatible with every account of knots; it decides nothing about storage or about the periphery.
treatment.strongestObjection: Rat brain, fast timescales, no history dependence: the finding shows vessels can nudge neurons now, not that they store anything and read it back later, and peripheral sensory endings have not been shown to do the same.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A peripheral demonstration that arteriolar caliber changes modulate sensory-ending activity through mechanosensitive channels.
Evidence of history-dependent, content-specific modulation (VASO-R005).

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review of slow-breathing studies in healthy humans documents reproducible increases in respiratory sinus arrhythmia and heart-rate variability consistent with a parasympathetic shift (VASO-E009, strong); the essay's uncited restatement (VASO-E036) adds nothing. The evidence is global cardiovascular indices in people with no tender point in the study; local, site-specific effects have never been measured.

treatment.plainLanguage: Breathing slowly, especially with a long exhale, reliably tilts the body's automatic nervous system toward its calming branch.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Both the vascular and the conventional accounts predict this global shift; it becomes diagnostic only if a local, breath-gated release is shown on top of it.
treatment.strongestObjection: Everything measured is on the heart; nothing shows the shift unlatching a specific vessel at a specific point, and the one pressure-only protocol cleared points without breath instruction.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Pressure during an inhale-and-hold failing to clear points that pressure during slow exhalation clears (VASO-R020).
Equal clearance under held breath, which would leave the global shift real but locally irrelevant.

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review found manual trigger-point examination not demonstrated reliable or valid, with no accepted reference standard (VASO-E011, strong); the Quintner–Bove–Cohen critique argues the construct rests on circular reasoning (VASO-E010), answered by a rebuttal so the exchange is the debate's state. Proponent groups concede the point in their own words — palpation is the reference standard and subjective (VASO-E029); no gold standard, inter-observer variability not improved by training, and imaging confirmed 71.5% of palpated spots (VASO-E078, VASO-E079, VASO-E081).

treatment.plainLanguage: Examiners cannot reliably agree on where a trigger point is, there is no agreed standard for what one is, and whether the construct is real at all is argued in the peer-reviewed literature.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Caps the observation base of every account equally: the stiffness, chemistry and EMG findings were all measured at sites chosen by a method not shown to be reproducible, so any decisive experiment must first solve blinded, instrumented localization.
treatment.strongestObjection: The reliability literature assesses the manual exam, not instrumented detection; blinded sonographers do image stiff regions at palpated sites, and imaging-anchored localization may escape the problem.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded inter-examiner reliability study with instrumented confirmation showing acceptable agreement.
A census with instrument-fixed sites finding stiffness and flow measures that pick out the palpated spots in unselected people (VASO-R002).

claimAssessments.reasoning: The claim's own admitted records are context only: Croft 1994 found two people reporting no pain with eleven or more examiner-elicited tender points at fixed sites, in a pain-selected subsample (VASO-E082), and the Ballyns introduction notes the syndrome is commonly recognized as 'muscle knots' (VASO-E109). The provisional grade leans, as a disclosed basis, on sibling records attached to other claims: blinded sonographers imaged graded stiff regions at palpation-selected sites in the trapezius (VASO-E087 on VASO-C182; VASO-E090 on VASO-C187) and imaging confirmed 71.5% of one examiner's palpated spots in the calf (VASO-E081 on VASO-C030). The critical report's caution that even the palpable spot is disputed is a provisional record this edition treats as absent.

treatment.plainLanguage: People do have small, discrete spots in muscle and fascia that are exquisitely tender when pressed.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The phenomenon every account explains; its being real decides nothing between them, and its being unreliable to locate weakens them all equally.
treatment.strongestObjection: About a quarter of what one examiner palpated as a knot had no imaging correlate, and the sites at which stiffness was imaged were chosen by the examiner first.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded census with instrument-fixed sites confirming, or failing to confirm, palpated tender points across unselected people (VASO-R002).
A reliability study showing palpated points are not reproducible even with imaging anchoring.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Every admitted record is context: a 1986 clinic-population estimate that myofascial pain affects about 23 million Americans, quoted second-hand in a 2011 introduction and concerning a pain syndrome rather than tender points in ordinary people (VASO-E108); the same introduction's remark that the syndrome is commonly recognized as 'muscle knots' (VASO-E109); and two pain-free individuals with high tender-point counts in a pain-selected community subsample (VASO-E082). No population count of palpable knots exists; the founding essay's report of ubiquity is a provisional record treated as absent. Weakly supported rather than unresolved because the research literature uniformly treats the phenomenon as common, but the frequency itself is unmeasured.

treatment.plainLanguage: Such tender points are supposed to be common — found in most people, not just patients — but nobody has ever counted.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The case's opening premise, not a discriminator: if knots turned out to be rare outside symptomatic people, the natural-history argument for stored tension would weaken for every account alike.
treatment.strongestObjection: The only prevalence figure is second-hand, forty years old, clinic-based and about a pain syndrome; the one community survey retrieved selected its examined sample on reported pain and so cannot speak to universality.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A knot census with pain-free controls and instrument-fixed sites across the age span (VASO-R002).
An unselected community tender-point survey retrieved with count distributions (VASO-R010).
A census finding tender points uncommon in people without pain.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hubbard and Berkoff recorded sustained spontaneous activity in a 1–2 mm nidus of every trapezius trigger point and none in adjacent non-tender fibers (VASO-E001, moderate). Simons 2002 qualifies exclusivity: endplate noise appeared at all 11 trigger-point sites, at 4 of 11 non-tender endplate-zone sites, and at no off-zone taut-band site (VASO-E031), so the claim is graded as the prevalence gradient it now states. The essay's restatement (VASO-E043) and the equine parallel from the unread second essay (VASO-E052) carry no independent weight.

treatment.plainLanguage: A needle in a trigger point picks up continuous electrical chatter in muscle that is supposedly at rest — more often there than at non-tender sites in the same nerve-supply band, and never where that band is absent.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Shows the knot is electrically maintained — state, not scar — but the signal is skeletal-muscle electrophysiology and lives in the endplate zone, so it fits stress-sensitive endplates as well as any vascular account.
treatment.strongestObjection: The signature tracks the endplate zone first and the trigger point second; Hubbard and Berkoff's silent control sites may simply have lain off the zone.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A repeat with a matched endplate-zone control site under mental arithmetic (VASO-R011).
A retrieved primary showing sympathetic blockade quiets the nidus (VASO-R009).
Endplate noise at non-tender endplate-zone sites as prevalent as at trigger points.

claimAssessments.reasoning: One study of fourteen subjects: mental arithmetic raised EMG activity at trapezius trigger points while control sites in the same muscle stayed comparatively quiet, without generalized tensing (VASO-E002, moderate); the essay's restatement (VASO-E033) adds no weight. Read beside the endplate-zone finding on the sibling claim (VASO-E031 on VASO-C002, a disclosed basis), the control site may not have been a matched endplate-zone site, so whether the stressor selected the trigger point or any endplate zone is open. Never replicated; no vascular measurement.

treatment.plainLanguage: Give someone a math test with a needle in a knot and the knot's electrical activity rises while nearby muscle stays quiet — a purely mental event turning up one tender spot.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The write half of any storage account, caught in motion — but the needle cannot tell stress-sensitive endplates, a sympathetic write to an intramuscular arteriole, and a regional skin vasoconstriction apart.
treatment.strongestObjection: A single small 1994 study from one lineage, with a control site that may have lain outside the endplate zone; sympathetic drive to spindles or endplates fits without any vessel.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Repeat with the endplate zone located electrically and the control needle in a matched non-tender endplate-zone site (VASO-R011).
A skin-perfusion camera showing a localized perfusion fall over the point during arithmetic and not over control skin.
A matched control rising as much as the trigger point.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone in SRC-JHONG-2026A, an unread self-published essay; no admitted evidence record. The mechanism it offers for the site-selective stressor result — regional sympathetic vasoconstriction written to a skin territory, as in blushing — is ordinary physiology stated as a reading, not a measurement at any tender point.

treatment.plainLanguage: The rival vascular account reads the math-test result as the brain blanching a patch of skin — a regional clamp on skin vessels — rather than as a write to muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Would relocate the addressability finding from muscle to skin, separating the perforator account from both the latch and the guarding readings, if a mental stressor produced a localized skin-perfusion fall over the point.
treatment.strongestObjection: Nothing has been measured; the EMG signal that motivates the claim was recorded in muscle, and stress-sensitive endplates explain it without any vessel.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Laser speckle or laser Doppler over a tender point during mental arithmetic showing a localized perfusion fall not seen over control skin (VASO-R016, VASO-R011).
Perfusion changes that are global or absent during the stressor.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The only record is the proponent's first-person report, in an essay whose text was AI-generated at the author's direction: press into a knot, exhale slowly, and something lets go in seconds (VASO-E014, weak). Consistent with widespread practitioner lore, contradicted by no one, measured by no one; expectation and attention cannot be excluded from any first-person release report.

treatment.plainLanguage: Press into a knot and breathe out slowly, and within seconds it feels as if something lets go.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Credible as an experience and worthless, on its own, as evidence about mechanism: a felt release is what every account predicts people will report, for different reasons.
treatment.strongestObjection: It is testimony, from the hypothesis's proponent, of a sensation; nothing shows a corresponding local event in the tissue.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-locked imaging of stiffness and perfusion at a felt release, exceeding sham sites and failed attempts (VASO-R001).
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition, or equal transitions at sham sites.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor, the essay's statement that pressure alone does not release a knot. Its one admitted record is context: a published pressure-only compression protocol carried no breathing instruction, recording or manipulation anywhere in its methods or results (VASO-E067). What that protocol achieved is held on a different claim — first-round sonographic disappearance of 60% of active and 86% of latent points (VASO-E072 on VASO-C005) — and is named here as a lead against the necessity of the breath, not spent as a grade: breathing was uninstructed, not held constant; the endpoint was undetectability over minutes, not a release in seconds; and the muscle and population differ from the practitioner reports.

treatment.plainLanguage: The 'two-key' rule: pressure finds a knot but does not release it; the release needs the exhale as well.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Decides whether the breath is a key at all: if held breath does not lower clearance, the releasing element need not answer to autonomic state and the cleanest argument for a vascular element falls; if inhale-hold blocks clearance, breath-gating is real.
treatment.strongestObjection: A protocol that told nobody how to breathe made most imaged trigger points undetectable in a single session of thumb pressure.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: The runners' protocol repeated with breathing recorded and randomized across free breathing, slow exhale and inhale-and-hold (VASO-R020).
Release of a knot by hydrodissection with no breath (VASO-R017).
Equal clearance under held breath — the claim false; clearance blocked by held breath — the claim true.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone — the founding essay's statement of the timing prediction — with no admitted evidence record. No study in the ledger has recorded perfusion and stiffness together at a release with time resolution; the one imaged within-session disappearance archived no cine loops and performed no Doppler.

treatment.plainLanguage: At a breath-assisted release, blood is predicted to come back first and the tissue to soften second.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The one timing prediction the vascular accounts make that neither guarding nor densification makes; observed, it would be the smoking gun, and stiffness leading or no perfusion change would cut against a vascular element.
treatment.strongestObjection: It is a prediction with no observation behind it, and a fast non-vascular state predicts the opposite ordering.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved Doppler and elastography across release events showing perfusion leading stiffness (VASO-R001).
Laser speckle at the surface showing a perfusion flash before any stiffness change (VASO-R016).
Stiffness falling with no perfusion change, or simultaneous change.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Chemistry: an acidic, mediator-rich milieu at active points, about nine volunteers, elevated at remote sites too (VASO-E006). Imaging: a 33-study review, characterized second-hand, reports stiffness and flow differences from healthy tissue (VASO-E007); Ballyns 2011 gives a group-level pulsatility difference (VASO-E022) and a graded stiff-area difference with active and latent above normal (VASO-E091, VASO-E090), classifiers for active versus normal (VASO-E096) and active versus latent (VASO-E099), and overall ROC separation (VASO-E100, VASO-E102), with the abstract's ROC listing as context (VASO-E101, VASO-E103). Qualified by the same source — indices that cannot classify sites (VASO-E025), no pain-free controls (VASO-E026) — and paralleled in the calf by active/latent differences within symptomatic runners with no control tissue (VASO-E068, VASO-E069, VASO-E070, VASO-E071, VASO-E072, context and qualifier). Second-essay restatements (VASO-E050, VASO-E051) and the essay's Doppler gloss (VASO-E042) carry no weight.

treatment.plainLanguage: Where an examiner finds a trigger point, instruments find something: more acid and pain chemicals, a stiffer patch of tissue, and somewhat different blood flow in nearby arteries.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: All three accounts predict these differences — guarding compresses the bed, densification stiffens, a throttled vessel starves — so they show a knot is something without saying what.
treatment.strongestObjection: Every comparison sits inside symptomatic muscle at palpation-selected sites, most from one NIH lineage; the flow indices do not classify sites and one shows no difference at all.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A census with pain-free controls and instrument-fixed sites showing whether stiffness and flow measures pick out palpated spots (VASO-R002).
Shear-wave replication of the stiff-area gradient in a second laboratory.
Imaging finding nothing at palpated spots in unselected people.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Preregistered within-subject experiments in 57 volunteers: attending to a histamine skin-prick site produced about 1.5-fold smaller and faster-resolving responses in about 90% of participants across two cohorts, with no difference in arousal measures and higher heart-rate variability under inward attention, dissected into sensory and vagal routes by lidocaine (VASO-E008, strong). Single laboratory, published 2026; the essay relays the authors' caveat that the route is vagal and skin is not parasympathetically innervated (VASO-E041).

treatment.plainLanguage: Simply paying attention to an inflamed patch of skin makes the inflammation smaller and shorter, without any change in stress arousal.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: An existence proof that cognition can write to a peripheral vascular bed at a chosen site — the channel the synthesis needs — but over tens of minutes by immune regulation, saying nothing about knots, smooth muscle or seconds.
treatment.strongestObjection: The demonstrated route is vagal anti-inflammatory regulation on a timescale of minutes in acute healthy skin; nothing connects it to a latch or a tender point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication in a second laboratory.
A seconds-scale, site-specific vascular effect of attention at a tender point.
Failure to replicate.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 reports a median pulsatility index of 8.3 near active sites against 3.0 near normal sites (VASO-E022, moderate), in vessels typically over a millimeter across within 1–2 cm of the point. Capped by the same source: no pain-free control group, 'normal' sites in symptomatic muscle, and the authors' statement that the findings do not represent normal variation (VASO-E026).

treatment.plainLanguage: Arteries near active trigger points show blood surging and falling more sharply with each heartbeat than arteries near palpably normal sites in the same muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The footprint proponents read as something clenched upstream, but its authors list contracture compressing the bed, trapezius anatomy, inflammation and transducer pressure as candidate causes and never mention latch.
treatment.strongestObjection: Conduit-scale vessels in symptomatic patients with no pain-free baseline; the index varied so widely it could not classify any individual site.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Doppler in pain-free controls establishing the normal baseline.
Microvascular flow measured in the muscle bed itself at a release.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 reports retrograde diastolic flow at 55% of active, 40% of latent and 31% of palpably normal sites (VASO-E022, moderate); the 'normal' sites sat at least 5 cm from trigger points in symptomatic muscle with no pain-free group, so the source cannot say whether 31% is baseline or spillover (VASO-E026).

treatment.plainLanguage: Backward flow between heartbeats — the sign read as a vascular footprint of a knot — also shows up near about a third of sites that feel normal in the same muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Cuts against the specificity of the vascular signature: the waveform is a gradient across symptomatic muscle rather than a marker of a knot.
treatment.strongestObjection: Without pain-free controls the 31% could be either the population baseline or the influence of neighbouring points.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A pain-free control series establishing how often retrograde diastolic flow occurs in normal trapezius.
Retrograde flow absent at palpably normal sites in a larger blinded series.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The abstract's means — 0.57 ± 0.20 cm² at active and 0.36 ± 0.16 cm² at latent sites — are recorded directly (VASO-E087, VASO-E089), with the ROC statement that area distinguishes the site classes (VASO-E104); the active-versus-latent significance (VASO-E093), the latent-versus-normal classifier (VASO-E106) and the calf parallel (VASO-E085) enter as context. Blinded sonographers, but one laboratory, one vibration frequency from an off-the-shelf massager, palpation-selected sites and the same NIH lineage as the biochemistry.

treatment.plainLanguage: On vibration elastography, the stiff patch at a spontaneously painful trigger point is larger than at one that hurts only when pressed.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A graded stiffness that tracks symptom class, which every account predicts — guarding graded with severity, or a bigger throttled territory.
treatment.strongestObjection: Single study, relative and frequency-dependent measure not confirmed as shear elasticity, at sites the examiner had already classified.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Shear-wave elastography replication in a second laboratory with instrument-fixed sites.
Failure of the gradient to appear when sites are fixed before palpation.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The normal-site mean of 0.17 ± 0.22 cm² is recorded from the abstract with the P < .01 across site types (VASO-E090), with the ROC separation statement (VASO-E104), the active-versus-normal classifier (VASO-E105) and the latent-versus-normal classifier (VASO-E107). The 'normal' sites lie in symptomatic muscle at least 5 cm from a trigger point; the standard deviation exceeds the mean, and no pain-free tissue was imaged.

treatment.plainLanguage: Palpably normal sites in the same muscle showed a much smaller stiff area than trigger points — but they were normal sites in a muscle that had a knot elsewhere.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Supplies the baseline for the stiffness gradient without supplying a healthy baseline; it decides nothing between mechanisms.
treatment.strongestObjection: There is no pain-free control tissue, and a standard deviation larger than the mean means some 'normal' sites carried stiff areas comparable to latent points.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Elastography of pain-free controls establishing what normal trapezius measures.
A blinded series in which normal-site areas overlap trigger-point areas.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Simons, Hong and Simons 2002 report endplate noise at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites outside any trigger point, against eleven of eleven trigger-point sites (VASO-E032, moderate); abstract only, nonrandomized, unblinded, ten subjects, from the construct's leading proponents — whose finding nonetheless cuts against exclusivity.

treatment.plainLanguage: The electrical chatter taken as a trigger point's signature also turns up, less often, at spots in the same nerve-supply band that are not tender at all.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Undermines the reading of the nidus as an exclusive, addressable island and places the signature in the endplate zone first; it favours the guarding account's localization without touching the vascular question directly.
treatment.strongestObjection: Small, unblinded and abstract-only; four of eleven is a minority, and the trigger point still carries the signature every time.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A blinded, larger series with electrically located endplate zones measuring prevalence and amplitude at matched sites (VASO-R011).
Endplate noise found to be as prevalent at non-tender endplate-zone sites as at trigger points.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The same study found no endplate noise at taut-band sites lying outside the endplate zone, in eleven of eleven muscles (VASO-E032, moderate), with the same limitations — abstract only, unblinded, ten subjects.

treatment.plainLanguage: A taut band of muscle that lies outside the nerve-supply zone shows none of the electrical chatter, however tight it feels.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Ties the signature to the motor endplate rather than to tautness or tenderness as such — the conventional skeletal-endplate reading — while saying nothing about vessels.
treatment.strongestObjection: A null in eleven sites from an unblinded study by proponents; the sites' distance from the endplate zone rests on the authors' electrical localization.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Spontaneous activity recorded at off-zone taut-band sites in a blinded replication.
Amplitude data showing the trigger-point signal differs in kind, not only in prevalence, from endplate noise elsewhere.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 states that no differences in resistivity index were detected between normal, latent and active sites, and that the pulsatility index was not a good classifier because of large variance (VASO-E024, moderate). A within-patient comparison in symptomatic subjects; the authors attribute the similarity partly to the proximity of normal sites to trigger points.

treatment.plainLanguage: A second standard measure of how hard blood has to push through the arteries near a trigger point showed no difference at all between knots and normal sites.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A negative result on the vascular footprint: the signature at real trigger points is partial, not categorical, which weakens any reading of the Doppler data as a throttled bed.
treatment.strongestObjection: Normal sites sat in the same symptomatic muscle, so a real difference could have been masked by proximity.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A resistivity difference emerging against pain-free control tissue.
Microvascular rather than conduit-artery flow measured at the point itself.
